question: How do Morgan Stanley and Merrill differ in how they segment clients by wealth tier?

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: Its Wealth Management segment provides a comprehensive array of financial services and solutions to individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and to businesses and institutions. The 2Q26 10-Q (period ended June 26, 2026) and 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) state this.

Morgan Stanley: Its U.S. Bank Subsidiaries provide loans to a variety of customers, including high to ultra-high net worth individuals, as well as large corporate and institutional clients. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states they accept deposits, provide loans to a variety of customers, including large corporate and institutional clients, as well as high to ultra-high net worth individuals, and invest in securities.

Morgan Stanley: Within the Wealth Management business segment, tailored lending consists of bespoke lending arrangements provided to ultra-high net worth clients. The 2Q26 10-Q (period ended June 26, 2026) states other loans primarily include certain loans originated in the tailored lending business within the Wealth Management business segment, which typically consist of bespoke lending arrangements provided to ultra-high net worth clients.
Morgan Stanley: It offers family office infrastructure solutions for ultra-high net worth clients. The 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026) states this.

Morgan Stanley: In Asia (Hong Kong), it serves high-net-worth wealth businesses. The 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025) references high-net-worth wealth businesses, which have had a great run here in Hong Kong.
Merrill: It presents a 'Wealth Continuum' that segments clients into Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM) and High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM) tiers. The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.

Merrill: Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business is focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states its advisory business provides a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets.

Merrill: Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, together with Bank of America Private Bank, targets high net worth and ultra high net worth clients. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.
Merrill: It serves 750K households with $500K+ in assets. The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.
Merrill: It serves 54K households with $10MM+ in assets. The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.

Merrill: Merrill defines its households as households with $250K+ in investable assets, excluding stock plan and banking-only households. The 3Q26 earnings deck (September 30, 2026) and October 14, 2026 press release state Merrill includes households with $250K+ in investable assets, excluding stock plan and banking-only households.
Merrill: In 3Q26, it added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%. The 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026) states this.
Merrill: It reports 750K households with $500K+ in assets and 54K households with $10MM+ in assets. The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.

Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank defines its relationships as relationships with $3MM+ in total balances, including third-party activities and excluding irrevocable trust-only, institutional philanthropic, and exiting relationships. The 3Q26 earnings deck (September 30, 2026) and October 14, 2026 press release state this.
Merrill: In 3Q26, the Private Bank added 470 net new relationships with at least $3 million under management. The 3Q26 earnings call (October 2026) states this.

Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, targets high net worth and ultra high net worth clients. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.

Morgan Stanley: It describes its Wealth Management segment as providing financial services and solutions to individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, as well as businesses and institutions. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.

Morgan Stanley: It describes CRE loans in Wealth Management as generally benefiting from guarantees from high or ultra-high net worth clients. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.

Merrill: It labels its wealth tiers within a framework it calls the 'Wealth Continuum,' which includes the tiers 'Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)' and 'High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM).' The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.
Merrill: It identifies household wealth tiers of '$500K+ households' (750K) and '$10MM+ households' (54K). The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.
Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank relationships are defined as those with $3MM+ in total balances. The 3Q26 earnings deck (September 30, 2026) states this.

Merrill: Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets, providing tailored solutions through investment management, brokerage, banking and retirement products. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.

Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, provides comprehensive wealth management solutions targeted to high net worth and ultra high net worth clients, including customized solutions for wealth structuring, investment management, trust and banking needs. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.

Merrill: It offers robust solutions for ultra-high-net-worth clients, including alternative investments and sustainable and impact investing strategies. Merrill's recruiting website (page content as of November 3, 2026) states this.

Merrill: A team specializing in serving high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients joined Merrill Private Wealth Management and is aligned with Merrill's Southeast private wealth division, indicating private wealth management serves that client tier. Trade press (published September 8, 2026) reports this.
Merrill: Merrill Wealth Management reports 750,000 households with $500K+ in assets. The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.
Merrill: Merrill Wealth Management reports 54,000 households with $10MM+ in assets. The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.
Merrill: It added approximately 3.3K net new $500K+ households in 1Q26. The April 15, 2026 press release states this.
Merrill: It added approximately 5.4K net new $500K+ households in 2Q26. The July 14, 2026 press release states this.
Merrill: It added approximately 4.2K net new $500K+ households in 3Q26. The October 14, 2026 press release states this.
Merrill: It added approximately 18K net new households in FY25. The January 14, 2026 press release (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.
Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank added approximately 280 net new relationships with $3MM+ clients in 1Q26. The April 15, 2026 press release states this.
Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank added approximately 430 net new relationships with $3MM+ clients in 2Q26. The July 14, 2026 press release states this.
Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank added approximately 470 net new relationships with $3MM+ clients in 3Q26. The October 14, 2026 press release states this.
Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank added approximately 1,600 net new relationships with $3MM+ clients in FY25. The January 14, 2026 press release (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.

Morgan Stanley: It describes its Wealth Management business as serving individual investors 'including high and ultra-high net worth individuals,' but the passages disclose no specific dollar thresholds or formal tier definitions for these wealth tiers. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.

Morgan Stanley: It refers to 'ultra-high net worth clients' in describing its tailored (bespoke) lending arrangements within Wealth Management, without giving a dollar threshold for that tier. The 2Q26 10-Q (period ended June 26, 2026) states this.
Merrill: It presents a 'Wealth Continuum' that segments clients into Mass Affluent ($500K-$1MM) and High Net Worth ($1MM-$10MM) tiers. The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.
Merrill: It serves 750K households with $500K+ in assets and 54K households with $10MM+ in assets. The November 5, 2025 investor day deck states this.
Merrill: It includes households with $250K+ in investable assets, excluding stock plan and banking-only households. The 3Q26 earnings deck (September 30, 2026) states this.

Merrill: Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, provides solutions targeted to high net worth and ultra high net worth clients. The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states this.

The two firms' wealth tier segmentation schemes differ: Merrill uses an explicit, dollar-thresholded 'Wealth Continuum' (Mass Affluent $500K-$1MM and High Net Worth $1MM-$10MM, with additional breakpoints of $250K for investable assets, $500K+ and $10MM+ households, and $3MM+ in total balances at Bank of America Private Bank), whereas Morgan Stanley describes serving 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals' without disclosing any specific dollar thresholds or formal tier definitions. These schemes are therefore not comparable on the same basis: Merrill's tiers are defined by explicit asset breakpoints, while Morgan Stanley's tier references carry no dollar thresholds in the passages searched.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley: Its Wealth Management supports clients through three channels—Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace—rather than segmenting by wealth tier; advisor assignment is described by channel, with the Advisor-Led channel being accounts that have a Wealth Management representative assigned. The 2Q26 10-Q (period ended June 26, 2026) states this.
adjacent.differs_because: Morgan Stanley segments clients by service channel (Advisor-Led, Self-Directed, Workplace) and by whether a Wealth Management representative/advisor is assigned, not by wealth tier; the passages contain no wealth-tier thresholds (e.g., $1M, $10M+) or tier-specific service models.
